latin.517: §. VII. SECULI TERTII Professor Veritatis Eucharisticæ primus TERTULLIANUS meritô suô inducitur, quippe ipso Seculi initio in flore constitutus, unâque ac eâdem sententiâ tàm Verborum Eucharisticorum Christi: Hoc est corpus meum, improprietatem disertissimè confessus, quam veram nihilominus veri corporis Christi in cœna præsentiam testatus.
latin.518: At inquit, Christus acceptum panem & distributum Discipulis, Corpus suum illum fecit, dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum, i. e. FIGURA CORPORIS MEI; Figura verò non fuisset, nisi VERITATIS FUISSET CORPUS: Res enim vacua, ut est phantasma, figuram capere non potest. Contra Marcionem lib. 4. c. 40.
latin.519: Quanquam Idem Tertullianus, alibi, nempe Libro de Resurrectione Carnis, etiam præsentiam corporis Christi in Eucharistia ferè corporalem inculcasse legatur, scribens: Caro (nostra) corpore & sanguine Christi vescitur, ut & anima de Deo saginetur: Id quod ceteris Patris hujus, jure alioquin venerandi, erroribus, vel in vulgus eruditorum notis, annumerandum eô fuerit, quia vel ipsi Transsubstantiatores, à nutritione carnis nostræ propriè dicta per corpus Christi, in S. cœna sumtum, omninò abhorrent, ut suprà diximus.
latin.520: Rectius Seculi ejusdem Doctor proximus, utut non minus, ob allegoricas Scripturarum Interpretationes justo crebriores, erroribus aliquot exstantioribus scatentes, quàm ob multarum Veritatum sacrarum expositionem verè sublimem, famâ inter Theologos celebratus, ORIGENES puta, non improprietatem tantùm verborum Christi: Hoc est corpus meum, unà cum præsentia corporis Christi reali, in S. Cœna, ad exemplum Tertulliani, stabilivit, sed verò prætereà hanc corporis Christi præsentiam, quin & participationem, merè Spiritualem urget esse; de priori, ita adversus Marcionitas arguens: Quod si Christus (ut obloquuntur Marcionitæ) carne destitutus erat & exsanguis, cujusmodi Carnis, cujus corporis, qualis tandem sanguinis signa & IMAGINES PANEM ET POCULUM MINISTRAVIT. Dialog. 3. de Homine Christo.
latin.521: De posteriori autem Homil. 7. in Leviticum hacce commentatus: Agnoscite, quia figura sunt, & ideo tanquam spirituales, non carnales, examinate & intelligite, quæ dicuntur; si quasi Carnales accipitis, lædunt vos & non alunt! Est enim in Evangelio Litera, quæ occidit eum, qui non spiritualiter, quæ dicit, ea advertit. SI ENIM SECUNDUM LITERAM SEQUERIS, HOC IPSUM QUOD DICTUM EST: NISI MANDUCAVERITIS CARNEM MEAM ET BIBERITIS SANGUINEM MEUM, OCCIDIT HÆC LITERA.
latin.522: Tertius denique & jam altius seculum hoc ingressus, divus CYPRIANUS, veram illam ac spiritualem corporis Christi in Eucharistia præsentiam atque participationem, disertissimè omnium, rhetoricô interim stylô (hôc potissimum tempore à Patribus excoli cœptô, facilè autem in abusum trahendo, in sermone de Lapsis populari, Rhetoricæ per se suamque naturam, indulgere solito) inter alia hunc in modum edisserit, dum nempe in eos invehitur, qui ab negatâ semel fide christiana, paulò post leniori pænitentiâ tacti, sicque minus præparati, ad S. cœnam accedunt: Mortiferos, ait, idolorum cibos adhuc penè ructantes, exhalantibus etiamnum scelus suum faucibus & contagia funesta redolentibus, Domini Corpus invadunt. Et iterum. Spretis his omnibus atque contemtis, vis infertur Corpori Christi & sanguini ejus; plus modò in Dominum manibus atque ore delinquunt, quàm cùm Dominum negaverunt. Hinc namque corpus Christi invadere, & huic, nec non Sanguini ejus, vim inferre aliter, quàm Spirituali modô, haud poterant, sumentes nempe Panem & Vinum, seu Sacramentum Domini, ab impiis non nisi per Sacrilegium, usurpandum & attrectandum.

pass_a.517: §. VII. Of the THIRD age the first Professor of Eucharistic Truth, TERTULLIAN, is deservedly brought on, being established in flower at the very beginning of the age, and in one and the same sentence having most expressly confessed both the impropriety of Christ’s Eucharistic Words This is my body, and nonetheless attested the true presence of Christ’s true body in the supper.
pass_a.518: But, he says, Christ made that bread which He had taken and distributed to the Disciples His Body, saying: This is my body, i.e. THE FIGURE OF MY BODY; But it would not have been a Figure unless it had BEEN A BODY OF TRUTH: For an empty thing, as a phantasm is, cannot take a figure. Against Marcion book 4 ch. 40.
pass_a.519: Although the same Tertullian elsewhere, namely in the Book on the Resurrection of the Flesh, is also read to have inculcated a nearly corporal presence of Christ’s body in the Eucharist, writing: Our flesh is fed with the body and blood of Christ, that the soul also may be fattened from God: Which is to be numbered among the other errors of this Father, otherwise rightly venerable, or among those known to the learned public, for even the Transsubstantiators themselves wholly abhor a properly so-called nutrition of our flesh by Christ’s body taken in the Sacred supper, as we said above.
pass_a.520: More rightly the next Doctor of the same age — Origen, celebrated among Theologians as much for a truly sublime exposition of many sacred Truths as he is not less full of certain more outstanding errors because of allegorical Interpretations of the Scriptures justly too frequent — not only established, after Tertullian’s example, the impropriety of Christ’s words This is my body together with the real presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper, but moreover urges that this presence of Christ’s body, nay also the participation, is merely Spiritual; on the former arguing thus against the Marcionites: But if Christ (as the Marcionites object) was destitute of flesh and bloodless, of what sort of Flesh, of what body, of what blood finally did He minister the signs and IMAGES BREAD AND CUP? Dialogue 3 on the Man Christ.
pass_a.521: But on the latter commenting thus in Homily 7 on Leviticus: Recognize that they are figures, and therefore examine and understand what is said as spirituals, not carnals; if you receive them as Carnals, they hurt you and do not nourish! For there is in the Gospel a Letter which kills him who does not attend spiritually to what it says. FOR IF YOU FOLLOW ACCORDING TO THE LETTER, THIS VERY THING WHICH WAS SAID: UNLESS YOU SHALL HAVE EATEN MY FLESH AND DRUNK MY BLOOD, THIS LETTER KILLS.
pass_a.522: The third finally, and already having entered this age more deeply, holy CYPRIAN, most expressly of all sets forth that true and spiritual presence and participation of Christ’s body in the Eucharist — meanwhile in a rhetorical style (begun to be cultivated by the Fathers especially at this time, yet easily drawn into abuse, as in the popular sermon On the Lapsed, wont to indulge Rhetoric for itself and its nature) — among other things in this manner, while he inveighs against those who, having once denied the Christian faith, shortly after touched by milder penitence and so less prepared, approach the Sacred supper: Still almost belching, he says, the death-dealing foods of idols, with jaws still exhaling their crime and smelling of deadly contagions, they invade the Lord’s Body. And again. All these things despised and contemned, violence is done to the Body of Christ and His blood; now they offend more against the Lord with hands and mouth than when they denied the Lord. Hence indeed they could not invade Christ’s body, and do violence to it and His Blood, otherwise than in a Spiritual mode, namely taking Bread and Wine, or the Sacrament of the Lord, which the impious are not to usurp and handle except through Sacrilege.

517: §.VII opens the THIRD century with Tertullian as first professor of Eucharistic truth — in flower at the age’s start.
In one sentence he both confesses the impropriety of Christ’s words ‘This is my body’ and attests the true presence of Christ’s true body in the supper.
518: Contra Marcionem 4.40: Christ made the bread taken and given to the disciples His Body by saying ‘This is my body’ — that is, the FIGURE OF MY BODY.
It would not be a figure unless it were a BODY OF TRUTH: an empty phantasm cannot take a figure.
519: Elsewhere (De Resurrectione Carnis) Tertullian seems to push a nearly corporal presence: our flesh is fed with Christ’s body and blood so the soul may be fattened from God.
Count that among his otherwise venerable errors — even Transsubstantiators wholly abhor proper nutrition of our flesh by Christ’s body taken in the supper.
520: Next, Origen (same century): with Tertullian he stabilizes the impropriety of ‘This is my body’ and real presence — then urges that presence and participation are merely Spiritual.
Against Marcionites: if Christ had no flesh and blood, of what flesh and blood did He minister bread and cup as signs and IMAGES?
521: Origen Hom. Lev. 7: recognize they are figures — examine them as spiritual, not carnal; taken carnally they hurt and do not nourish.
The Gospel letter kills whoever does not hear spiritually: if you follow ‘Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood’ according to the letter, that letter kills.
522: Cyprian, later in the century, most expressly teaches true spiritual presence and participation — in rhetorical style (On the Lapsed) against the unprepared who still reek of idol foods yet invade the Lord’s Body.
They can invade Christ’s body and do violence to His blood only in a Spiritual mode — by taking bread and wine, which the impious handle only by sacrilege.

notes.519: Nearly corporal error; Transsubst. also reject.
